summary: An announcement that SRI-ARC produced a Quick Reference Card for TNLS, the terminal version of NLS. It covers basic commands, TIP settings for reaching SRI-ARC, basic TENEX commands, and view specification codes. A copy would go to each station agent, with more on request.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC announces a quick reference card for TNLS. It lists what the card covers and how a site can request extra copies.

subtitle: An announcement of a quick reference card for TNLS users.

tldr.problem: TNLS users needed a compact reference for basic commands and special-purpose features.
tldr.mechanism: SRI-ARC produced a card covering everyday TNLS commands, TIP settings, TENEX/EXECUTIVE commands, and viewspecs.
tldr.outcome: One copy was to be sent to each station agent; sites could contact SRI-ARC to request additional copies.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 496's status as Unknown. The RFC announces a printed reference card for TNLS users.

sections.title: The TNLS Quick Reference Card
sections.content: RFC 496 announces a new Quick Reference Card for TNLS. The card documents basic commands used in everyday TNLS work and some special-purpose features.
sections.plainLanguage: SRI-ARC made a quick reference card for TNLS users. The card covers basic commands and selected special features.

sections.title: What the Card Covers
sections.content: The card includes TIP settings for connecting to SRI-ARC, basic TENEX/EXECUTIVE commands, and a complete set of VIEWSPECS codes for TNLS use. The RFC does not reproduce the card's command list or explain individual codes.
sections.plainLanguage: The reference covers network connection settings, basic system commands, and viewspec codes. The announcement does not list the codes themselves.

sections.title: Distribution
sections.content: The notice says one copy of the card will be sent to each station agent. People who want copies for users at their site are asked to contact Marcia Keeney at SRI-ARC and state how many they need.
sections.plainLanguage: Each station agent was to receive one card. A site could request more copies for its users.
